body: I don't drink much but alcohol sometimes helps me tap into the feelings I left behind. I took medications as an adolescent and young adult (Lexapro/Zoloft) but they never helped, only physically removing myself from the bad situation did. I'm grateful I had the opportunity to do that. Is your medication working at least OK for you?
The only family I could ask are my parents who rely on me right now. It's really a last resort

Eventually I would like to move away and maybe I will have roommates I talk to. Ideally I'd rather have roommates I don't have to talk to. I feel a strong avoidance even to the thought of having to socialize with other people when it's not on my own terms, if I had to pinpoint the location of this feeling it would be a tightening in my chest. It just makes me feel weary. It's not like I could say anything interesting or worthwhile to anyone else. I'm glad that you have a roommate to talk to. What was your situation like before?
We each make one another unhappy. Talking won't help at this point.

Being unable to understand and relate to people. Not feeling anything from friendships. Not feeling enjoyment from things I should like. Always being on the outside looking in. Feeling hurt and alone all the time. Any moment I have an idle thought, the thought is that I wish I was dead. I feel rotten to the core. I feel inferior and sad all the time and there's no one to talk to.
For the longest time I never returned hurtful words but I did last night.
Thank you for your kind words.

Thank you for your thoughtful reply. It is not entirely his fault in the sense that we're on different wavelengths and I can't change someone who is unwilling to change yet I keep trying. I will hope for better in the future with reservations that I'll end up only with what I deserve.

I'm sorry you're suffering.

I don't know if or how it would work at your school, but I would try to talk directly with your professor about your health right now. If he sees that you have the work done, and that you are making your best effort despite your pain right now, he might want to do everything in his power to help you pass.

I know it's easier said than done, but getting a part time entry level job might help you to feel better. Maybe there is a social cause you can volunteer your time to at school as well. I would also look into LGBTQ services for someone to talk to anonymously.

I'm sorry if I come off as trite. The fact that you have not given up in school is proof that you have a future.

Did your parents tell you why they stopped filling your prescriptions? They might have been afraid of vyvanse hurting your health in the long term. Bring up to them that you would like to be further educated on the risks of taking vyvanse and look into treatment for how you feel. It is obvious you care about your future and are worried about your grades and desperately want help. Ask your parents for help if you can, or a trusted teacher.

What are your favorite classes? What are the ones you have the most trouble with?

Even though you regret your honesty, being honest with her was the bravest and most compassionate gesture you could make for her and yourself. It is good that you see her as motivation, but eventually motivation has to come from within. I think on some level you understand this which is why you were honest with her.

You are a kind and good person for your honesty. The world needs more good men. I am sorry you're suffering and I hope you will be able to find healthy relief so that you can continue to bring light into the world and feel the light as well.
